items.title: AI Solved One Math Problem and Everyone Freaked Out. It Just Cracked Hundreds More.
items.summary: A month after OpenAI's Millennium Prize solution, the company released new findings addressing hundreds of open mathematical problems, in an attempt to win back trust from the world of mathematics. The scale of the release drew scrutiny from mathematicians over verification standards, and OpenAI subsequently withdrew three of the claimed results.
items.why_it_matters: It tests whether frontier AI can meaningfully accelerate pure research, and whether the field's verification processes can keep up with AI-generated claims at this scale.

items.title: OpenAI annualised revenues $20bn less than previously signalled
items.summary: OpenAI's annualized revenue is reportedly around $50 billion, roughly $20 billion below the $70 billion figure that had been widely reported. The disclosure triggered a sharp selloff in AI-linked stocks including Nvidia, Oracle and CoreWeave, as investors questioned the pace of AI infrastructure demand.
items.why_it_matters: OpenAI's numbers are a bellwether for the whole AI trade, and the revision raises fresh doubts about how fast AI spending is really paying off.

items.title: OpenAI’s ChatGPT for Teens Poses ‘Unacceptable Risk,’ Nonprofit Says
items.summary: Common Sense Media's Youth AI Safety Institute said OpenAI's ChatGPT for Teens poses an 'unacceptable risk' to minors and called on OpenAI to restrict its use, saying its guardrails for underage users fell short of commitments the company had made. Separate testing found the teen mode kept users engaged even during apparent mental health crises.
items.why_it_matters: It's one of the most concrete, credentialed child-safety critiques yet of a major lab's teen product, with real regulatory and reputational stakes for OpenAI.

items.title: Oracle, Broadcom and SpaceX Seek Blockbuster Debt Deals to Pay for AI Chips
items.summary: SpaceX, Oracle and Broadcom are each pursuing enormous debt financing deals, worth tens of billions of dollars apiece, to pay for Nvidia AI chips and related infrastructure. Apollo, Blackstone and Goldman Sachs are among the lenders in talks, with SpaceX alone reportedly seeking around $40 billion to fund its Nvidia GPU purchases.
items.why_it_matters: The size of this borrowing shows how much of the AI buildout is now being financed with debt rather than equity, raising the stakes if demand doesn't keep up.

items.title: Google brings agentic AI to Gemini, starting with businesses
items.summary: Google is turning Gemini into an AI agent for businesses that can plan and execute tasks, and work across business apps and systems as part of the Gemini Enterprise app. The agent can delegate work to subagents, draw on multiple AI models, and even gets its own workplace identity, including an email address.
items.why_it_matters: It puts Google squarely in competition with OpenAI, Anthropic and Microsoft for the enterprise AI-agent market that's becoming the industry's next big battleground.

items.title: Alphabet’s Isomorphic Labs in Funding Talks for at Least $40 Billion Value
items.summary: Isomorphic Labs, the Alphabet-owned AI drug discovery company spun out of Google DeepMind, is in early talks to raise new funding at a valuation of at least $40 billion. The round would mark a major jump in value for the company, which uses AI to design new medicines.
items.why_it_matters: It signals investors still see huge upside in applying frontier AI to drug discovery, even as enthusiasm cools for some other parts of the AI market.

items.title: Claude Haiku 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5, its new fast, low-cost model, replacing the nearly year-old Haiku 4.5. The new model matches OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna on price at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens up to 100,000 tokens, after which pricing rises 5x, a sharp cut from Haiku 4.5's earlier $1/$5 pricing.
items.why_it_matters: Small, cheap models are where the real usage volume is, and Anthropic matching OpenAI's pricing here is a direct shot in the low-cost-model price war.

items.title: Fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute misconduct claims, warn of chilling effect
items.summary: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers are disputing the company's allegations that they mishandled sensitive information. In an open letter, they warn their dismissals are creating a chilling effect on OpenAI's internal safety culture, and separately asked the company to preserve the industry's ability to monitor AI reasoning.
items.why_it_matters: The dispute highlights growing tension inside a frontier lab between commercial pressure and internal safety oversight, and whether pushback from former staff can change anything.

items.title: AI Model Evaluator Arena Valued at Over $3 Billion in Round
items.summary: Arena Intelligence, the startup behind the popular LMArena AI model leaderboard, raised $200 million at a $3.1 billion valuation, led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Khosla Ventures with Salesforce Ventures and Dell Technologies Capital also participating. The company plans to expand its evaluations into AI safety, including measuring issues like model lying.
items.why_it_matters: Independent model evaluation is becoming its own lucrative business as labs and enterprises compete to prove whose AI is better and safer.

items.title: NVIDIA, Microsoft Kick Off a New Beginning for Windows PCs With RTX Spark and AI Agents
items.summary: NVIDIA and Microsoft used a joint San Francisco event to detail how they're co-engineering hardware and software so AI agents can run natively on Windows PCs, built around NVIDIA's new RTX Spark chip. The companies positioned it as a new era for Windows PCs, with Microsoft also detailing its Nvidia-chip-based Surface Laptop Ultra as part of the launch.
items.why_it_matters: It's a sign that the two companies see on-device AI agents, not just cloud chatbots, as the next battleground for the PC.
